title_en: Having a Minions Movie Marathon in 2026 Requires at Least 3 Streaming Subscriptions
body_en:
The Despicable Me movie franchise has been a hit since 2010, but it's the Minions themselves that have captured everyone's heart. These mischievous little yellow underlings have been in more movies than Gru at this point, so I think it's safe to say the Despicable Me films are part of the larger Minions universe .
With the release of Minions & Monsters in 2026 , there are now a total of seven of these movies available to watch at home. IGN gave the latest film an 8 out of 10 , proving that those little banana-loving dudes have still got it even after all this time.
However, if you're looking to watch every movie in the franchise, you unfortunately won't be able to find them all on a single streaming platform.
All of the Minions movies are created by Illumination , which means they are all owned by Universal Studios. So when these films first come to a streaming service, it's almost always going to land on Peacock first . But that doesn't mean every movie stays on Peacock. To have yourself a Minions movie marathon, you're going to need a myriad of streaming subscriptions at your disposal.
There aren't currently any Blu-ray box sets you can buy that include all of the Minions movies. There is, however, a 10-movie Illumination collection that will get you four of them. This collection was released back in 2020, so it only includes up to Despicable Me 3 and the first Minions spin-off film. You can get the collection at Gruv, which is one of the best places to buy Blu-rays these days.
Minions & Monsters won't be released on Blu-ray until September 8 , so there likely won't be any new box sets for the franchise announced until after that.
Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics -- from TV series to books and the latest Pokémon games .
